bullets.title: INTC: Massive Q2 Beat, Capex Inflects Hard — Transformation in Progress
bullets.body: Intel posted its strongest revenue growth in 15+ years with 2Q26 revenue of $16.1B (beat consensus of $14.3B), EPS of $0.42 doubling Street estimates, and DCAI segment up 24% QoQ at 39.5% OPM. 3Q26 guided at $16.3B, also above consensus, but capex is inflecting to >$20B in FY26 and 'significantly above' in FY27, keeping FCF near breakeven and raising dilution risk. Citi maintains Buy at $130 PT; Wolfe models $5 EPS power at $100 stock and is skeptical; MS raised PT to $84 from $75 on foundry progress; one analyst sets $136 PT on 5x 2027E BVPS.

bullets.title: AMD: AI Day Raises TAM Dramatically; Jefferies Lifts PT to $640
bullets.body: AMD raised its 2030 AI accelerator TAM to ~$1.4T (from ~$500B by 2028) and DC server CPU TAM to ~$220B (>50% CAGR, from $120B); Helios rack ships end-Q3, broad ramp 4Q26-1H27. OpenAI and META each committed to deploy 6GW of MI450s; Anthropic targeting 1GW in 2027. Jefferies raised PT to $640 from $515 (Buy); Truist maintains Buy at $478; RBC stays Sector Perform at $540 pending Helios execution proof. HBM4 supply deal with Samsung described as 'imminent.'

bullets.title: CHTR: Q2 Earnings Miss on Broadband, FCF — Stock Hits 52-Week Low, Down ~12% Premarket
bullets.body: Charter Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $5.45B came in below consensus of $5.58B; broadband net losses of -172K wider than expected; broadband ARPU fell 1.5% YoY to $70.16; FCF of $969M well below the ~$1.3B estimate. Mobile net adds of 406K beat. Citi maintains Buy at $190 PT (50% upside) on FCF inflection thesis but acknowledges near-term pressure; CHTR stock hit a 52-week low at $123.70, -68.9% from its 52-week high. Cox synergies target $800M-$1B, capex declining to $7.5-8B by 2028, buybacks resume Q4.

bullets.title: VZ: Q2 Postpaid Beat, Guidance Raised — Citi Buy at $55 PT
bullets.body: Verizon posted postpaid phone net adds of 184K (consensus 106K), EPS of $1.30 beating estimates, and FCF of $6.4B well above the $5.5B estimate. Revenue of $34.3B missed $35.17B estimate; FWA broadband adds of 193K also light. Company raised FY26 EPS guidance to $4.99-$5.04 (from $4.95-$4.99) and bumped share repurchase target to $4.5B from $3.5B. AI Connect fiber initiative with Google dark fiber deal expected to generate 'multiple billions' starting FY27. Citi maintains Buy with $55 PT (25.5% upside + ~6% yield).

bullets.title: DLR: Strong Q2, Double-Digit FFOPS Growth Guidance — TD Cowen Upgrades to Buy
bullets.body: Digital Realty beat Q2 with strong retail and hyperscale bookings; development pipeline now >$20B (54% pre-leased) targeting 10%+ yields; rent backlog up 40% QoQ to $1.4B. Management raised guidance to double-digit core FFOPS growth through 2027-2028 (vs. prior high-single-digit). TD Cowen upgraded to Buy at $222 PT; Citi remains a buyer; JPMorgan OW at $235 PT citing supply-demand imbalance and NIMBYism constraining new capacity.

bullets.title: CHTR/CMCSA: Cable Sector Under Pressure — Broadband ARPU Erosion the Key Overhang
bullets.body: Charter's Q2 broadband ARPU miss and wider-than-expected losses dragged CMCSA down 2.1% in sympathy premarket. Wells Fargo cut CMCSA PT to $23 (from $28) on slower broadband recovery; RBC and KeyBanc note no cable co has grown both EBITDA and broadband subs simultaneously. Street skews 35% Buy / 55% Hold / 10% Sell on CMCSA; consensus FY27 EPS cut $0.06 to $3.62. Peacock reached profitability in Q2 (FIFA/NBA) but expected to flip negative in Q4.

bullets.title: Bitcoin Miners (HUT, WULF, CIFR, RIOT): MS Bullish on AI Data Center Conversion
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Stephen Byrd is bullish on bitcoin miners converting to 'Powered Shell Providers' for hyperscaler AI campuses. HUT signed a 15-year deal at 17% yield/$17/watt; WULF signed a 20-year deal at 18% yield/$19/watt — both well above the $2-4.5 EV/Watt at which miners currently trade. CIFR has >2GW in ERCOT queue; RIOT expected to sign at least one major deal at Corsicana or Rockdale in 3Q26. MS initiated HUT and RIOT at Overweight.

bullets.title: Mag 7 Week Ahead: MSFT, META, AAPL, AMZN Earnings Next Week; ~30% FOMC Hike Priced
bullets.body: Peak earnings week next week with all four remaining Mag 7 names reporting; July FOMC meeting also concludes Wednesday. Markets now pricing ~30% chance of 25bp rate hike (up from 12% a week ago) driven by oil near $100/bbl and rising inflation concerns. Premarket Mag 7 snapshot today: TSLA +1.3% (partial bounce after -15% Thursday), MSFT +1.1%, GOOGL +0.7%, META +0.7%, AMZN +0.5%, AAPL +0.2%, NVDA -0.4%.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Anthropic Stake Valued at ~$124B; AI Positioning Note
bullets.body: Google's stake in Anthropic is now valued at approximately $124B. Separately, Citi's TMT consensus note flags GOOGL and AAPL as having 'recently swapped positions on the AI leaderboard driven by capex strategies'; Citi rates both Buy. GOOGL stock was down ~7% Thursday on capex guidance despite 80% cloud revenue growth and strong GCP performance.

bullets.title: META: Standalone Marketplace App Launched — Negative Read for EBAY/ETSY
bullets.body: Citi flags META rolling out a standalone 'Seller' marketplace app featuring 430M items and 44M vehicles globally, which is characterized as negative for EBAY and ETSY. Separately, META's $12B Texas data center financing cleared at 7%+ yield, 40bps tighter than its Louisiana deal, though Goldman warns AI bond repricing is 'punitive for equity multiples.'

bullets.title: TEAM: Citi Reiterates Buy at $110 PT — 28-29% Cloud Growth Expected
bullets.body: Atlassian is down >50% YTD but Citi argues fundamentals are healthier than the stock price implies, reiterating Buy at $110 PT and projecting 28-29% cloud growth. TEAM was +1.6% in premarket trading.

bullets.title: OMC: Q2 Earnings Preview — Consensus +3.6% Organic Growth, Options Imply ~8.8% Move
bullets.body: Omnicom reports Q2 earnings July 28 after close. Consensus calls for $6.44B revenue, $2.67 EPS, and +3.6% organic growth at 18.2% adjusted EBITA margin. OMC has beaten revenue and EPS consensus 17 of the past 20 quarters. Stock is +3.3% since late April vs. S&P +5.0%; options imply ~8.8% move.

bullets.title: INTC AI vs. AMD Competitive Dynamics: AMD MI500 Claims Optical Interconnect Edge
bullets.body: Reports circulating that AMD's upcoming MI500 features optical interconnects and is ahead of NVIDIA's Rubin Ultra in HBM technology, 4-die packaging, and scale-up domain. This follows AMD's AI Day where OpenAI and META each committed to 6GW MI450 deployments. Intel's DCAI segment grew 59% YoY in 2Q with ASP gains from higher core count mix; foundry 14A committed to HVM in 2028.

bullets.title: ORCL: Hits 52-Week Low at $117.30, Down 51.5% from High; $3.31B Navy Contract
bullets.body: Oracle hit a fresh 52-week low at $117.30, down 2.3% on the session and 51.5% from its 52-week high. Partially offsetting: ORCL was awarded a $3.31B US Navy contract, sending shares up ~1.9% in premarket from the prior close. MS TMT credit team had flagged early caution on ORCL with CDS trade recommendation.

bullets.title: TMUS: Q2 Selloff Overdone — JPM and MS See Attractive Entry at 7x EV/EBITDA
bullets.body: T-Mobile sold off 10.8% after Q2 earnings despite beating estimates; shares now trade at a 5-year low multiple of ~7x EV/EBITDA. MS and JPM both flag the selloff as overdone; TMUS raised FY26 adjusted FCF/OCF guidance by $200M. Citi stays neutral citing churn friction from rate plan modernization and satellite LEO (Starlink) valuation overhang.

bullets.title: MU/SNDK Memory Selloff: MS Joe Moore Sees Compelling Dip-Buy Entry
bullets.body: Memory stocks (MU -2.0%, SNDK -2.8% premarket) are selling off, but Morgan Stanley's Joe Moore argues DC purchasing checks reveal an increasingly compelling entry point. Memory is characterized as 'THE bottleneck' to AI builds, with DC memory prices up 25%+ in 3Q and HBM4 demand robust with NVDA Rubin content doubling. Shortage expected to intensify 2027-2028.

bullets.title: MSFT: Building In-House AI Image Models (MAI) to Replace OpenAI — 85% Cheaper
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes Microsoft is replacing OpenAI's image generation models with its own in-house MAI models, described as 85% cheaper to run. This follows reports of MSFT's PC Xbox backward compatibility hiding an internal emulator, but the MAI development is the more meaningful strategic signal for the AI cost-efficiency narrative.

bullets.title: CRM: VA Awards $1.6B, 3-Year Contract; +1.5% Premarket
bullets.body: Salesforce received a $1.6B, 3-year contract from the VA, helping shares gain 1.5% in premarket trading.

bullets.title: T: MS Raises PT to $27 — Double-Digit Adj EPS CAGR Through 2028
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised its price target on AT&T to $27 (implying ~17% upside) citing strong wireless net adds, ARPU growth, churn reduction, and a projected double-digit adjusted EPS CAGR through 2028.

bullets.title: APH: Q2 Earnings Preview July 29 — 20/20 Beat Record, Options Imply ~14% Move
bullets.body: Amphenol reports Q2 earnings July 29; consensus expects $8.26B revenue (above $8.1-8.2B guidance) and $1.18 EPS (above $1.14-1.16 guidance) at 27.6% adjusted operating margin. APH has beaten both revenue and EPS consensus in all 20 of the past 20 quarters. Stock is +9.5% since late April; options imply ~14% move.
